samples.summary: applyLayoutProps collects splices that can overlap; applying them highest-first then corrupts the file
samples.evidence: `for (const s of splices.sort((a, b) => b.start - a.start)) out = spliceSpan(out, s.start, s.end, s.text);` assumes the collected spans are disjoint, but nothing enforces that. Two reachable overlaps: (a) `classOps` splices the className string literal while `sets: [{name:'className', value:null|'x'}]` splices the enclosing attribute span — the inner splice is applied first and changes the length inside the outer span, so the outer splice (computed from ORIGINAL offsets) cuts the wrong region, e.g. `<div className="a">` with `additions:['p-2']` + `className: null` yields `<divp-2">`, an unparseable file; (b) two `sets` entries with the same `name` produce two identical [start,end) spans and the second replacement is applied over already-rewritten text. Both write `located: true` and a corrupt file to disk.

samples.summary: insertImport merges into a type-only import, producing invalid syntax or a value imported as a type
samples.evidence: The target is chosen purely by module specifier (`st.moduleSpecifier.text === spec.module`) with no `importClause.isTypeOnly` check — extract.mjs:481 shows the flag is otherwise tracked in this package. For `import type { Props } from './m'`, `spec.default` splices at `clause.getStart(sf)` (inject.mjs:804), and the ImportClause of a type-only import starts at the `type` keyword, yielding `import React, type { Props } from './m';` — a parse error in the consumer's file. With `named`, the new binding is merged into the type-only group, so a value (`Button`) becomes a type import and the consumer's build fails with "refers to a type but is being used as a value". A file having both a `import type {...}` and a value import from the same module hits the first match, which may be the type one.

samples.summary: The `sets` path can overwrite a non-literal className, defeating the guard the classOps path implements
samples.evidence: `classOps` refuses when `classLiteralOf` returns null ('className is not a string literal'), specifically so `className={t("nav.home")}` is not clobbered. But `sets` uses only `findJsxAttribute(node, set.name)` and replaces the whole attribute span with `renderAttribute(...)`, with no special case for `className`. `sets: [{name: 'className', value: 'p-2'}]` therefore rewrites `className={t("nav.home")}` to `className="p-2"`, destroying the expression — exactly the loss the classOps branch's comment says the module refuses to risk.

samples.summary: `structuralEditable` no longer mirrors resolveNode after the `role: 'container'` widening, so the newly-allowed insert stays gated off
samples.evidence: extract.mjs:537 states this flag 'MIRRORS resolveNode(…, {requireStatic: true}), GUARD FOR GUARD' and 'is what enables "insert sibling" / "remove" in the outline'. The diff relaxes two of those guards for containers in resolveNode, but `structuralEditable` still requires `owner === node && !returnedJsx.includes(node)`, and no container-specific flag was added (types.ts:116 has only `structuralEditable`). So the capability the change exists to unblock — insert a child into the returned root or into a `{cond && <div/>}` element — is still reported as non-editable to the client, and the mirror comment is now inaccurate.

samples.summary: Misleading / missing reason when the classOps create path hits a node with no tag name
samples.evidence: In the 'no className attribute at all' branch, when `additions.length` is non-empty but `tagNameOf(node)` is null (a fragment), control falls to `else if (!unsafe.length)` and reports 'no className attribute to remove classes from' — which is wrong for an add request; and when `additions` is empty AND some tokens were unsafe the caller gets only the reject note. The equivalent `sets` path does emit a specific 'cannot add X to a fragment'.

`removeImport` accepts `{module, named, default}` in its JSDoc but only inspects `namedBindings`: `if (!nb || !ts.isNamedImports(nb) || !wanted.size) return { located: false, reason: 'nothing removable' }`. A caller asking to drop an unused default binding gets 'nothing removable' and the import is left in place, and the whole-statement branch (`drop.length === nb.elements.length && !target.importClause?.name`) can never fire when a default exists, leaving `import D, {  } from 'm'`.

verdict.reason:
Verified in-repo: `applyLayoutRemove` splices `[childSpliceOffset(...) , node.getEnd())` (inject.mjs:715-722), and `childSpliceOffset` returns `prev.owner.getEnd()` for index>0 (inject.mjs:331-332) — the end of the previous *numbered* sibling. `childrenOf` numbers only JSX-yielding children and explicitly excludes JsxText, comments, and expressions yielding no JSX (jsx-nodes.mjs:289-296, 336-353, 360-364; `pushExpr` contributes nothing for a bare identifier). Therefore removing `` from `
{label}
` deletes `{label}`, silently dropping the interpolation; same for prose text between elements. No guard prevents this: resolveNode's requireStatic guards only cover non-static scope, owner!==node (expression container), and top-level returned elements (jsx-nodes.mjs:844-896), and applyLayoutRemove only refuses root nodes and empty parentPath (inject.mjs:682-708). The design doc sanctions over-capture of leading newline/indent only (design-editor-engine.md:861-864), not sibling content, and the involution test passes because both directions share the over-captured span. Real data loss on a common JSX shape via an exported API — critical under the correctness rubric.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. childSpliceOffset (inject.mjs:331-332) takes the offset from kids[index-1].owner.getEnd(). Owner sharing is real: pushChild forwards the {…} JsxExpression as owner (jsx-nodes.mjs:352) and pushExpr pushes both ternary branches (jsx-nodes.mjs:390-393) and both binary operands (385-388) with that same owner and unchanged 'static' scope. applyLayoutInsert resolves the parent with role:'container', which explicitly bypasses the owner!==node refusal (jsx-nodes.mjs:859-871), and the only other check is the range test index>kids.length (inject.mjs:616), which admits index 1 and 2 for a two-child ternary. Both indices therefore resolve to the same offset — after the closing '}' — so the node lands after B and the actual child index differs from the requested one, returned as located:true with no note (inject.mjs:656-657). The remove path is guarded (test at inject.test.mjs:356-361), but no guard covers inserting between owner-sharing siblings, and no test exercises it. Silent wrong placement plus an off-by-one for later path-based anchors is a real logic bug in the correctness lane.

finding.summary: applyLayoutProps collects splices that can overlap; applying them highest-first then corrupts the file
finding.evidence: `for (const s of splices.sort((a, b) => b.start - a.start)) out = spliceSpan(out, s.start, s.end, s.text);` assumes the collected spans are disjoint, but nothing enforces that. Two reachable overlaps: (a) `classOps` splices the className string literal while `sets: [{name:'className', value:null|'x'}]` splices the enclosing attribute span — the inner splice is applied first and changes the length inside the outer span, so the outer splice (computed from ORIGINAL offsets) cuts the wrong region, e.g. `<div className="a">` with `additions:['p-2']` + `className: null` yields `<divp-2">`, an unparseable file; (b) two `sets` entries with the same `name` produce two identical [start,end) spans and the second replacement is applied over already-rewritten text. Both write `located: true` and a corrupt file to disk.

verdict.reason:
The described code is present exactly as quoted: applyLayoutProps collects splices with ORIGINAL-file offsets and applies them highest-start-first (inject.mjs:567-570, spliceSpan at :71-72) with no disjointness, containment, or dedupe check. Overlap (a) is concrete: classOps pushes the inner className string-literal span (:442) while a `sets` entry with value:null pushes the enclosing attribute span (:499-504); for `
x
` with additions ['p-2'] + className:null, the literal span [15,18) is spliced first (grows 4 chars) and the outer span [4,18) then cuts the wrong region, yielding `x` returned with located:true (:575). Overlap (b) is also real: the sets loop (:491-526) never dedupes by name, so two entries for the same existing attribute push identical spans (:514) and the second replacement is applied over already-rewritten text of different length. No guard elsewhere prevents it — findJsxAttribute (:353-364) merely locates the attribute, rewriteClassLiteral (:184-238) only validates tokens, and grep across packages/design-editor/src shows no intent validator/schema for `sets` (the only consumer is this loop). This is a data-corruption / broken-invariant bug that writes an unparseable file while reporting success — critical/major impact in the correctness lane.

verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as described. insertImport selects its merge target purely by module specifier (inject.mjs:769-778, break on first match) with no importClause.isTypeOnly check — the flag is tracked elsewhere in this package (extract.mjs:481, 492), so its absence here is an omission. Three concrete correctness failures follow: (a) the default splice at clause.getStart(sf) (inject.mjs:804-805) lands before the `type` keyword of a type-only clause, emitting `import React, type { Props } from './m';`, which does not parse; (b) the named path (inject.mjs:812-829) only checks ts.isNamedImports and appends into the type-only group, turning a requested value binding into a type import so the consumer build fails with "refers to a type but is being used as a value"; (c) if the type-only group already lists the name, `have.has(n)` filters it and line 845 returns located:false 'already imported', silently omitting the value import — precisely the failure mode the function's own comment at lines 783-787 says it exists to prevent. Writes corrupted source into a consumer working tree, per the file header at inject.mjs:10-15.

verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as described. inject.mjs:445-457 refuses a classOps edit when `className` is not a plain string literal, with a comment naming `className={t("nav.home")}` and the translation-key loss it avoids. The `sets` loop at inject.mjs:491-526 looks the attribute up by name only (findJsxAttribute, :353-364), renders `name="value"` via renderAttribute (:508, :401-402), and splices over the whole attribute span `existing.getStart(sf)..existing.getEnd()` (:514) with no className special case — so `sets: [{name:'className', value:'p-2'}]` overwrites a `className={expr}` and destroys the expression. I searched for an upstream guard: this package has no intent dispatcher/validator (src/server contains only extract/inject/jsx-nodes/stamp plus types.ts), and the only `sets` call sites are tests, none of which constrain the attribute name. No guard makes the path unreachable, so I cannot name a refutation ground. Data loss / overwrite of authored source is explicitly in the correctness lane, and this module writes to the consumer's working tree, so it is blocking. The only mitigating fact is that no in-repo client currently sends `className` in `sets`, which is absence of a caller, not a guard.
